clinician.final_diagnosis: good recovery of venous stroke who was a carrier of a unique homozygous mutation, FVL
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old girl presented with a 4-month history of increasing chronic holocranial headache and visual blurring, which progressed to nocturnal and continuous headache. Examination revealed bilateral papilledema and reduced visual acuity. MRI of the brain showed a linear filling defect in the superior sagittal sinus. Genetic testing identified a homozygous Factor V Leiden (FVL) mutation. The patient was treated with heparin, followed by a 6-month course of coumarin, leading to complete resolution of cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT). At 3-year follow-up, she had no complaints, an unremarkable neurological examination, and intact visual acuity, indicating a good recovery.
